entities.summary: Stephen (I) Báncsa was the first Hungarian cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church. Prior to that, he served as Bishop of Vác from 1240 or 1241 to 1243, then Archbishop of Esztergom from 1242 until his creation as cardinal.

A prominent figure in the ecclesiastical hierarchy of medieval Hungary, Báncsa played a crucial role in shaping the country's religious landscape during the 13th century. He was born in the early 13th century, but the exact date remains unknown, and his early life is shrouded in mystery.

Báncsa's appointment as cardinal was a significant event, marking the first time a Hungarian had held this rank in the Catholic Church. His subsequent influence on the Church's policies and practices in Hungary had a lasting impact on the country's religious identity.
